description: Manage your Kubernetes clusters without bloat and telemetry

summary.one_liner: Rune is a fast native macOS Kubernetes cluster manager focused on day-to-day troubleshooting, with logs, YAML editing, port-forwarding, and metrics in one keyboard-friendly app.
summary.what_it_does: Rune is a macOS app for browsing and debugging Kubernetes clusters. It provides sections for workloads, networking, storage, config, RBAC, events, Helm releases, and a terminal view, with a toolbar for choosing context and namespace. Pod logs and unified service/deployment logs support search, time presets, previous logs, tail mode, container selection, and export as .log or ZIP. YAML can be edited with syntax highlighting and validation, then applied after a server dry-run and diff preview. It also offers port-forwarding, exec workflows, pod and node metrics when the cluster exposes them, and an Auth Doctor that checks permissions. Clusters can be added through kubeconfig discovery, pasted or imported files, manual token kubeconfig, or guided EKS, AKS, and GKE import.
use_cases: debug failing pods and read their logs
edit and apply Kubernetes YAML safely
port-forward to a pod or service
browse clusters with limited RBAC permissions
import kubeconfig files for EKS, AKS, or GKE
explore a Kubernetes UI without a server
notable: Unified logs across related pods with search, export as ZIP, and per-pod splitting
Server dry-run and diff preview before any YAML apply, with copyable kubectl command
Auth Doctor checks kubeconfig, namespace, logs, exec, and port-forward permissions
Manual namespace entry and per-context namespace favorites for RBAC-restricted clusters
Built-in in-memory demo cluster that needs no API server
caveats: Requires macOS 14 or later and Swift 6 to build
Source-available license: business use requires a paid commercial license or Mac App Store purchase
Metrics only work when the cluster exposes them
